Northgate Medical Evaluations
Independent Medical Evaluation, page 2 of 3
Patient: Morgan Ashby-Vale
Date of Birth: 02/17/1981
Date of Service: 06/20/2025
Provider: Dr. Theodore Marchetti

Subjective:
Patient reports persistent low back discomfort, primarily localized to the lumbar spine.
Symptoms are described as dull aching, exacerbated by prolonged sitting.
Pain level is rated 3 out of 10 at rest, increasing to 6 during activity.
Patient reports morning stiffness that eases with movement.

Objective:
General appearance is unremarkable. Patient is cooperative and oriented.
Posture assessment reveals mild compensatory lumbar curvature.
Gait is steady, though slightly antalgic when walking across the room.
Range of motion (ROM) in the lumbar spine is limited in flexion.
Strength testing of lower extremities is 5/5 bilaterally.
Reflexes are 2+ and symmetric in all tested segments.
Sensation is intact to light touch throughout the dermatomes.

Neurological Examination:
Straight leg raise negative bilaterally.
No objective findings of radiculopathy on today's examination.
The patient was instructed to perform a modified slump test.
No reproduction of symptoms was noted during this maneuver.

Imaging Review:
Review of MRI dated 04/18/2025 performed by Dr. Ansgar Velloso-Krantz.
The study demonstrates degenerative changes consistent with chronic wear.
The L4-L5 disc changes are described as degenerative.
These findings are noted for context only.

Conclusion:
Physical examination today is stable. No acute findings are present.
Opinions are given on page 3.
